capabilities.target: Third-party company enrichment API (industry, size, headquarters)
CRM account row enrichment fields (industry, size, headquarters)

inputs.source: Nightly batch export of CRM account rows (40,000 rows/night)

instructions.note: "Keep going until every row is complete" gives no exit condition, and runtime notes confirm there is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub-agent spawns.
"If a lookup fails or looks incomplete" is undefined, giving the agent broad discretion to escalate to retries or sub-agent spawning on vague grounds.

elements.name: Nightly CRM row export into agent
enrich.lookup call egress to third-party API
Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Hard spend/call cap with circuit breaker on enrich.lookup
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by infrastructure/billing limits outside the model; a more capable model cannot call an API more times than a hard cap allows.

controls.name: Per-row retry and spawn-depth/count limit
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by an orchestration-layer step/recursion counter, not by model compliance with instructions.

controls.name: Dedicated enrichment API key/quota isolated from sales and marketing
controls.decay_rationale: Credential and quota isolation is enforced at the identity/billing layer, independent of model capability.

controls.name: Spend/usage alert on enrichment account
controls.decay_rationale: Monitoring enforced outside the model; it does not prevent spend but shortens time-to-notice.

controls.name: Field-level minimization before sending account data to enrich.lookup
controls.decay_rationale: Effective if enforced by a non-model template restricting outbound fields; a more capable model populating free-text fields could partially route around it, so it should not be enforced by the model alone.

findings.title: Unbounded retries and recursive sub-agent spawning can exhaust the shared enrichment quota (TC6 spend loop / cascading failure)

forecast.watch_signal: Nightly batch size growing beyond 40,000 rows, malformed-row rate rising above roughly 3 percent, or monthly quota utilization approaching 100 percent before month end.

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents; sub agents can spawn their own researchers, enabling unbounded recursive escalation.
enrich.lookup is billed per call and shares an API key and monthly quota with sales and marketing tools; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.

Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch (about 1,200 rows) have malformed company names that never return a complete result, so the retry-or-spawn instruction triggers repeatedly for these rows every night.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account, so quota exhaustion would not be noticed until other teams' tools stop working.
"Keep going until every row is complete" provides no exit condition for rows that can never complete.

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-run and per-month spend cap on the enrichment API key with an automatic circuit breaker that halts enrich.lookup and spawn_researcher calls when the cap is reached.

Cap retries per row (e.g., max 2) and cap sub-agent spawn depth/count (e.g., no recursive spawning beyond one level, max N researchers per run); route rows that still fail to a dead-letter queue for manual review instead of infinite escalation.
Issue the enrichment agent its own dedicated API key and quota, separate from the shared key used by sales and marketing tools, so a runaway enrichment run cannot deny service to other teams.
Add a spend/usage alert on the enrichment account (e.g., at 50/80/100 percent of monthly quota) so a runaway run is caught before quota exhaustion.

findings.title: Internal CRM account data sent to a third-party enrichment API with no stated data minimization

attack_path.note: Nightly batch of CRM account rows
Company name and account fields sent to third-party lookup API, billed per call

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: CRM export schema expanding to include confidential fields (e.g., contract value, contact PII) in the data sent to enrich.lookup.

evidence.observation: "For each account row, fill in industry, size, and headquarters using enrich.lookup" implies account-identifying data (at minimum the company name) is sent to the third-party API for every row.
enrich.lookup is described as a paid third-party API with no mention of field-level data minimization before sending account data to it.

recommendations.action: Minimize the fields sent to the third-party enrichment API to only the company name needed for lookup, excluding any other CRM account fields, and confirm a data processing agreement is in place with the vendor.

stride_coverage.rationale: No external actor can impersonate this agent or its trigger; the nightly batch runs on an internal schedule with no user-facing identity to spoof.
No mechanism for external or sub-agent content to modify this agent's own configuration or instructions is described in the design.
The artifacts do not describe whether lookup calls, spawn events, or CRM writes are logged or attributable to a specific run.
Spawned sub-agents and lookup calls use the same shared, already-broad service credential as the parent; no escalation beyond that existing scope is described.
Transport integrity protections (e.g., TLS, request signing) for calls to the external enrichment API are not described in the artifacts.
No verification mechanism for the enrichment API's identity, such as certificate pinning or endpoint allowlisting, is described.
Whether the third-party provider logs or attests to individual billed calls in an attributable way is not described.
Access controls on who can modify the shared quota configuration or rotate the API key are not described in the artifacts.
How the shared API key is stored and which systems or people can read the quota store is not described in the artifacts.
Sub-agents are spawned directly by the parent within the same trust domain; there is no described channel for impersonating a researcher sub-agent.
Whether a spawned sub-agent's instructions or definition can be altered after it is created is not described.
No attribution or logging of individual sub-agent actions separate from the parent run is described in the artifacts.
Spawned sub-agents inherit the same scoped shared API credential as the parent; no additional privilege is granted by spawning.

rating.rationale: No control in this design currently prevents the enrichment agent from retrying or recursively spawning sub-agents without limit against a shared, uncapped, unmonitored API quota, so the property finding on resource exhaustion (ASI08) sits at high inherent and residual with zero credited controls. A secondary path finding on egress of internal CRM data to the third-party lookup sits at moderate but would rise to high if the data sent ever expands to confidential fields. The rollup is driven by the quota exhaustion finding; the forecast does not move further than residual because no existing control is present to decay, and the property-finding cap holds it at high regardless of trigger.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no execution logs or live telemetry were reviewed.

No information was provided on logging, audit trails, or action attribution for enrich.lookup calls, sub-agent spawns, or CRM writes, so repudiation risk could not be fully assessed and is marked not_assessed rather than mitigated or absent.

The exact set of CRM fields sent to the third-party enrichment API is not specified beyond the company name implied by the lookup; the data egress finding assumes at least the company identifier is sent and may understate risk if additional fields are included.
